questions.stem: 'Seit einem Jahr schreibe ich Bewerbungen, aber ich bekomme nur Absagen. Langsam verliere ich den Mut.' How does the writer feel?
options: Relieved to have more free time
Increasingly discouraged
Hopeful about a new offer
Angry with his old school
questions.explanation: 'Den Mut verlieren' means to lose heart, and 'langsam' shows it is happening gradually after a year of rejections ('Absagen'). Nothing suggests anger or relief.

questions.stem: What does 'die Langzeitarbeitslosigkeit' mean?
options: Working long hours
A long-term work contract
Long-term unemployment
Seasonal unemployment
questions.explanation: The compound is 'Langzeit' (long-term) + 'Arbeitslosigkeit' (unemployment). It usually describes being out of work for a year or more.

questions.stem: 'Wer keinen Schulabschluss hat, ist besonders häufig von Arbeitslosigkeit betroffen.' What does the sentence claim?
options: Unemployed people often go back to school to finish their studies
Most unemployed people have finished school with good results
Leaving school without a qualification has become very rare
People without a school qualification are especially often unemployed
questions.explanation: 'Wer keinen Schulabschluss hat' means 'anyone who has no school-leaving qualification', and 'betroffen von' means 'affected by'. The sentence links missing qualifications to a higher risk of unemployment.

questions.stem: 'Die Jugendarbeitslosigkeit ist in Deutschland niedriger als in vielen anderen EU-Ländern, was oft auf das duale Ausbildungssystem zurückgeführt wird.' What explanation does the text give?
options: Many young Germans leave to find work in other countries
The dual training system is often given as the reason
Strict laws stop employers from dismissing young staff
Most young Germans go to university instead of working
questions.explanation: 'Zurückführen auf' means 'to attribute to'. The text credits the dual system, in which trainees combine work in a company with vocational school.

questions.stem: What does 'die Perspektivlosigkeit' describe?
options: A feeling of having no prospects for the future
A refusal to see another person's point of view
A lack of skill in drawing and design
A short-sighted government policy
questions.explanation: 'Perspektive' here means prospects, and '-losigkeit' means 'lack of'. The word often comes up when young people see no chance of a job or training place.

questions.stem: 'Ein Nebenjob neben der Schule bringt nicht nur Geld, sondern auch erste Berufserfahrung.' Which benefits are named?
options: Free time and first work experience
Money and first work experience
Money and better marks at school
Work experience and new friends
questions.explanation: 'Nicht nur ... sondern auch' links two benefits: 'Geld' and 'erste Berufserfahrung'. Marks and friends are not mentioned.

questions.stem: What does 'das Rauschtrinken' mean?
options: Binge drinking
Drinking water quickly
Drink driving
Giving up alcohol
questions.explanation: 'Der Rausch' is intoxication, so 'Rauschtrinken' is drinking to get drunk, in large amounts in a short time. Drink driving is 'Trunkenheit am Steuer'.

questions.stem: In a report about addiction, what does 'Sie hat einen Rückfall erlitten' mean?
options: She relapsed
She fully recovered
She had a fall
She was arrested
questions.explanation: 'Der Rückfall' is a relapse, a return to the addiction after a period without it. 'Erleiden' means to suffer. A physical fall would be 'Sie ist gestürzt'.

questions.stem: What is 'ein Entzug' in the context of addiction?
options: A blood test that detects drugs after a party
A campaign warning against smoking
Treatment to stop using an addictive substance
A fine for possessing illegal drugs
questions.explanation: 'Der Entzug' (also 'die Entziehungskur') is withdrawal treatment: the body is weaned off the substance, often in a clinic. It comes from 'entziehen', to take away.

questions.stem: 'Viele Jugendliche unterschätzen die Gefahren, weil Alkohol überall erhältlich und gesellschaftlich akzeptiert ist.' Why, according to the text, do young people underestimate the dangers?
options: Alcohol is banned, which makes it exciting
Parents never talk to them about the risks of alcohol
There is no advertising for alcohol
Alcohol is easy to get and socially accepted
questions.explanation: The 'weil' clause gives two reasons: alcohol is available everywhere ('überall erhältlich') and accepted by society ('gesellschaftlich akzeptiert').

questions.stem: 'Natürlich gehört ein Glas Sekt an Silvester dazu, aber jedes Wochenende betrunken zu sein, ist etwas ganz anderes.' What is the writer's position?
options: Sekt should only ever be drunk on New Year's Eve
Occasional drinking is fine, but regular drunkenness is not
All alcohol should be banned, even on special occasions
Getting drunk every weekend is normal for most young people
questions.explanation: 'Natürlich ... aber' concedes one point and then contrasts it: a glass at New Year is accepted, being drunk every weekend is 'etwas ganz anderes'. The writer does not call for a ban.

questions.stem: What is 'eine Aufklärungskampagne'?
options: A law that bans a product outright
A campaign that informs people about a risk
A police operation to catch offenders
A concert that raises money for a drug charity
questions.explanation: 'Aufklärung' here means informing and educating people. An 'Aufklärungskampagne' about drugs explains the dangers so people can make informed choices.

questions.stem: 'Verbote allein bringen wenig. Wer Jugendliche wirklich schützen will, muss sie ernst nehmen und offen mit ihnen reden.' What does the writer argue?
options: Young people should be left to make their own mistakes
Talking about drugs only makes young people curious
Bans are not enough; open, respectful talk is needed
Stricter bans are the only way to protect young people
questions.explanation: 'Verbote allein bringen wenig' says bans alone achieve little, and the 'wer ... muss' sentence names the alternative: taking young people seriously and talking openly.

questions.stem: What is 'die Lohnlücke' between women and men?
options: The difference between their average earnings
The gap between the richest and poorest workers
Unpaid overtime worked by both groups
The time between two pay rises
questions.explanation: 'Die Lohnlücke' (also 'der Gender-Pay-Gap') is the gap between the average pay of women and men. 'Lohn' is wage and 'Lücke' is gap.

questions.stem: What is 'eine Frauenquote'?
options: A sports league that is only open to women and girls
A tax discount paid to working mothers
A required minimum share of women, such as on a board
The number of women in a country's population
questions.explanation: A 'Quote' is a quota, so a 'Frauenquote' sets a minimum proportion of women, for example among a company's directors or a party's candidates.

questions.stem: 'Frauen arbeiten häufiger in Teilzeit, oft weil sie Kinder oder Angehörige betreuen. Das wirkt sich später auf ihre Rente aus.' What consequence does the text describe?
options: Part-time work raising women's pensions
Lower pensions later because of part-time work
Children of part-time workers earning less as adults
Women retiring earlier than men do
questions.explanation: 'Sich auswirken auf' means 'to have an effect on'. Working part-time to care for children or relatives ('Angehörige') affects women's pensions ('Rente') later on.

questions.stem: What does 'Diskriminierung aufgrund der Herkunft' mean?
options: Discrimination because of someone's origin
Discrimination because of someone's age
Discrimination because of someone's income
Discrimination because of someone's religion
questions.explanation: 'Die Herkunft' is where someone or their family comes from. 'Aufgrund' + genitive means 'on the grounds of'.

questions.stem: 'Bei uns im Verein ist es egal, woher du kommst oder wie viel Geld deine Eltern haben: Auf dem Platz sind alle gleich.' What does the speaker value about the club?
options: The club has many wealthy members who support it
Only people from the local area are allowed to join the club
Membership costs nothing for anyone who plays well
Everyone is equal, whatever their background or wealth
questions.explanation: 'Es ist egal, woher du kommst oder wie viel Geld ...' means origin and money do not matter, and 'Auf dem Platz sind alle gleich' says everyone is equal on the field.

questions.stem: What does 'Er setzt sich für die Rechte von Menschen mit Behinderung ein' mean?
options: He explains the law to people with disabilities
He campaigns for the rights of people with disabilities
He sits on a committee for people with disabilities
He works as a carer for people with disabilities at home
questions.explanation: 'Sich einsetzen für' means 'to stand up for' or 'campaign for'. It has nothing to do with sitting, despite 'setzen'.

questions.stem: 'Mädchen können genauso gut programmieren wie Jungen. Trotzdem entscheiden sich deutlich weniger Frauen für ein Informatikstudium.' What point does the writer make?
options: Women are under-represented in computing despite equal ability
Girls are better at programming than boys at school
Hardly any young men choose to study computing
Women choose computing more often than any other university subject
questions.explanation: 'Genauso gut ... wie' says ability is equal, and 'trotzdem' introduces the contrast: far fewer women ('deutlich weniger Frauen') choose to study computer science.

questions.stem: 'Wir Jugendlichen müssen mit den Folgen des Klimawandels am längsten leben. Deshalb wollen wir mitreden.' What is the main argument?
options: Young people should leave all climate decisions to the scientific experts
Young people will live longest with the effects, so they want a say
Young people cause most of the damage, so they must change most
Older people are not affected by climate change at all
questions.explanation: The first sentence gives the reason (young people live longest with the consequences) and 'deshalb' introduces the claim: they want to have a say ('mitreden').

questions.stem: What does 'der Leistungssport' mean?
options: Sport watched on television
Competitive sport at an elite level
Sport played just for fun
Sport taught in school PE lessons
questions.explanation: 'Leistung' means performance or achievement, so 'Leistungssport' is high-performance, competitive sport. Sport for fun is 'Freizeitsport' or 'Breitensport'.

questions.stem: 'Viele junge Leistungssportler trainieren über 20 Stunden pro Woche. Für Freunde, Schule und Erholung bleibt da kaum Zeit.' What is the writer's concern?
options: Twenty hours a week is too little training to succeed
Young athletes spend too much time with their friends
Schools give young athletes far too much homework to finish
Training leaves little time for friends, school and rest
questions.explanation: 'Da bleibt kaum Zeit' means hardly any time is left over. The writer worries that the training load crowds out friends, school and recovery ('Erholung').

questions.stem: 'Montags Klavier, dienstags Fußball, mittwochs Nachhilfe ... Ich habe keinen einzigen freien Nachmittag.' What problem is described?
options: The speaker's lessons are always cancelled
Too many fixed activities leave no free time
The speaker cannot decide on a hobby
The speaker has stopped all after-school activities
questions.explanation: Listing a fixed activity for each day and saying there is not one free afternoon describes 'Freizeitstress': a timetable so full that leisure itself becomes stressful.

questions.stem: 'Fitness-Apps zählen jeden Schritt. Doch wer nur noch auf Zahlen achtet, verliert leicht den Spaß an der Bewegung.' What is the writer's view?
options: Fitness apps make exercise more fun for everyone
Counting steps is the best way to become fit
Apps should replace sport lessons at school
Focusing on numbers can take the fun out of exercise
questions.explanation: 'Doch' signals a reservation: whoever only pays attention to numbers easily loses the enjoyment of exercise. The writer is not against apps as such, only against fixating on the figures.

questions.stem: 'Viele Schüler lassen das Frühstück ausfallen und wundern sich dann, warum sie sich in der dritten Stunde nicht konzentrieren können.' What does the writer suggest?
options: Breakfast makes students sleepy in their morning classes
Lessons start too early for most students
Skipping breakfast harms concentration at school
Students should eat during the third lesson
questions.explanation: 'Ausfallen lassen' means to skip. The slightly ironic 'wundern sich dann' implies the cause is obvious: no breakfast, no concentration.

questions.stem: What does 'das Burnout' mean?
options: A high fever that lasts several days
Sunburn from too long on the beach
Exhaustion caused by long-term stress
A sports injury from overtraining
questions.explanation: German uses the English word for a state of emotional and physical exhaustion after prolonged stress, at work or at school.

questions.stem: What does 'das Schönheitsideal' mean?
options: A competition to choose a winner
An ideal of beauty set by society
A beauty salon in a city centre
A cosmetic product for the skin
questions.explanation: 'Das Schönheitsideal' is the idea of beauty a society holds up as the model. It often comes up in discussions of social media and body image.

questions.stem: 'Ich ernähre mich vegetarisch, aber nicht aus Prinzip: Mir schmeckt Gemüse einfach besser.' Why is the speaker vegetarian?
options: Advice from a doctor
The cost of buying meat
Personal taste, not principles
Concern for animal welfare
questions.explanation: 'Nicht aus Prinzip' rules out ethical reasons, and 'Mir schmeckt Gemüse einfach besser' gives the real one: the speaker simply prefers the taste of vegetables.

questions.stem: What is 'ein Auslandsjahr'?
options: A year of national holidays and festivals
A gap year spent at home with family
A year of study at a foreign-language school at home
A year spent abroad, often at school or working
questions.explanation: 'Das Ausland' means abroad, so an 'Auslandsjahr' is a year spent in another country, for example on a school exchange.

questions.stem: 'Mein Austauschjahr in Hamburg war nicht immer einfach. Anfangs verstand ich kaum etwas, aber genau das hat mich selbstständiger gemacht.' What did the writer gain?
options: A permanent place at a school in Hamburg after the exchange
Greater independence from coping with difficulties
Perfect German within the first few weeks
A wish never to go abroad again
questions.explanation: 'Genau das' refers back to the difficulty of understanding at first, and 'hat mich selbstständiger gemacht' names the result: more independence.

questions.stem: For many young Germans, what does 'Work and Travel' mean?
options: A school excursion to visit local workplaces and businesses
Travelling abroad and doing casual jobs to pay for it
A business trip paid for by an employer
Commuting a long way to work each day
questions.explanation: German has borrowed the English phrase for travelling in a country such as Australia or New Zealand on a working holiday, funding the trip with short-term jobs.

questions.stem: Forum post: 'Last-Minute-Urlaub? Nie wieder! Das Hotel war eine Baustelle und am Strand lag Müll.' What is the tone?
options: Excited and grateful
Calm and neutral
Nostalgic and wistful
Disappointed and annoyed
questions.explanation: 'Nie wieder!' and the complaints about building works and rubbish show strong annoyance at a disappointing trip.

questions.stem: Which phrase introduces an argument against a proposal?
options: 'Dafür spricht, dass ...'
'Ein weiterer Vorteil ist, dass ...'
'Hinzu kommt, dass ...'
'Dagegen spricht, dass ...'
questions.explanation: 'Dagegen spricht' means 'what speaks against it is'. 'Dafür spricht' introduces an argument in favour, and the other two add a further point.

questions.stem: What does 'die Zivilcourage' mean?
options: Respect for the law and the police
The courage to stand up for others in public
The duty to do military service
Polite and helpful behaviour towards strangers
questions.explanation: 'Zivilcourage' is the courage to intervene or speak out in everyday life, for example when someone is being harassed, even at a personal risk.

questions.stem: 'Als ein Mitschüler im Bus beleidigt wurde, sahen alle weg. Nur Lena sagte laut, dass das nicht in Ordnung sei.' What does the text show about Lena?
options: She looked away like all the others
She reported the bus driver to the school
She spoke up when everyone else looked away
She was the one who insulted the student
questions.explanation: 'Sahen alle weg' means everyone looked away, and 'nur Lena' sets her apart: she said openly that it was not acceptable.
